summary: All five occurrences support predigen; preacher identity, religious tradition and exhortation content do not establish additional senses.
ʕal- consistently introduces the audience. The officer’s content can be a question-like clause about what Islam says; direct sermon material follows in other contexts.
Root-initial k must be distinguished from indicative k-: korazno after d- and korazwa need no extra indicative prefix; kkorəz has both. The new box is Infectum-wa, not ko-Preterit.
The Preterit and Infectum-wa base shapes are already compatible with krəzle/korəz. Their new boxes add attested form distribution, not a new stem or reconstructed paradigm.
Habitual German pflegte at the fox’s sermon is translated from Infectum plus a weekly expression. It does not turn that Turoyo form into Infectum-wa.

Round 2, Jan Beṯ-Şawoce. Supplied English is project machine translation [MT], not an edition translation; all semantic decisions are based on the Turoyo. Only this round’s proposals are encoded here. Round-1 proposals remain separate.
Jan confirms round-1 Preterit and Infectum-wa coverage rather than introducing those boxes anew. The secure new box is Imperativ kraz. Preterit additions stop at five cumulative examples.
ʕal- marks sermon audience or target; b tərki identifies language, bi ʕito location, and cognate karaze content. No separate senses are created for these participants.

Jan 2.11/2808 prints makrazle, an isolated III-shaped preaching form. Glossary form/search lookup found no matching makraz use. Context does not demonstrate causing another person to preach; no III stem is published pending verification.
Confirm the alternative PrS reference prs 226/20 = PrS 77/59 before replacing inherited source numbering; the fox’s Sunday sermon is kept as a single example.
Verify makrazle in Jan 2.11/2808 against the source and local paradigm: III formation, a source error, or another analysis? No unattested Infectum is reconstructed.
Confirm kurazno in Jan 2.31/5155 beside glossary korəz/korazno; preserve source vocalism. In /5154 does ʕal target mean preach to or against Nineveh?
